description: The card filter classified blank on the NUMERIC-ZEROS third disjunct while the account filter is valid: the controlled pair of case07, which reaches the same card-blank outcome through SPACES, and the card-side mirror of case12, which drives the identical disjunct on the account. 2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS sets INPUT-OK, FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID and FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID at :610-612, then normalises. This is where the case earns its place: :622-623 tests CARDSIDI OF CCRDSLAI = '*' OR = SPACES, and sixteen ASCII zero characters match NEITHER, so the ELSE at :625-626 runs and MOVE CARDSIDI TO CC-CARD-NUM lets the typed value SURVIVE into the work area intact - unlike cases 06, 07 and 11, where :624 replaces it with LOW-VALUES before the edit ever sees it. ACCTSIDI is likewise neither '*' nor SPACES at :615-616, so :619 moves the eleven typed digits into CC-ACCT-ID. 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT therefore SUCCEEDS: it sets FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :648, fails the not-supplied test at :651-653 on all three disjuncts because CC-ACCT-ID-N is 2 rather than ZEROS, fails IS NOT NUMERIC at :665 because the value is eleven digits, and runs the ELSE at :675-678, moving CC-ACCT-ID into CDEMO-ACCT-ID and setting FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID. It writes NO message, so WS-RETURN-MSG stays OFF - its 88 value is SPACES at :135 and :264 set it - and that is precisely what leaves the single message slot free for the complaint 2220 is about to raise. The account is valid deliberately for that reason; case06 shows the suppressed alternative, where 2210 fills the slot first and 2220's guarded MOVE never fires. 2220-EDIT-CARD then sets FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK at :688 and reaches the not-supplied test at :691-693, whose three disjuncts are CC-CARD-NUM EQUAL LOW-VALUES, CC-CARD-NUM EQUAL SPACES, and CC-CARD-NUM-N EQUAL ZEROS. The first two FAIL - the field holds sixteen 0x30 characters, which are neither binary zero nor blank - and the THIRD succeeds. That disjunct is expressed over CC-CARD-NUM-N, the PIC 9(16) item that REDEFINES the PIC X(16) CC-CARD-NUM at app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy:37-39, so it is a byte reinterpretation of ONE backing span through a second typed accessor and never a parse of a string into an int. The card is therefore judged blank NUMERICALLY while remaining non-blank ALPHANUMERICALLY, and the branch is unreachable without going through the -N view, which is exactly what makes this case the card pair's REDEFINES assertion (gate G34): the round trip holds in both directions over the same sixteen bytes, since CC-CARD-NUM-N reads as numeric zero while CC-CARD-NUM still reads back as the sixteen zero characters the operator typed. :694-695 then set INPUT-ERROR and FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK; IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :696 still holds, so :697 sets WS-PROMPT-FOR-CARD and the twenty-four characters of 'Card number not provided' reach WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75), right padded with fifty-one spaces, and then ERRMSGO PIC X(80) through :494 as twenty-four significant characters followed by fifty-six spaces. :700 moves ZEROES into CDEMO-CARD-NUM and :701 takes the GO TO, a forward early exit that becomes a plain Java return preserving evaluation order (rule R7) - so the numeric edit at :706 is NEVER REACHED. Sixteen zeros are numeric and would not have tripped it anyway, but the assertion is about the ordering, and a restructuring that evaluated both tests would reach the same outcome only by accident: 'CARD ID FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 16 DIGIT NUMBER' at :711 must not appear anywhere here, and its presence would prove the ZEROS disjunct was missed and the input fell through to the numeric test. Note the asymmetry between the two edits, preserved rather than tidied (practice B5): :676 moves CC-ACCT-ID, the alphanumeric X(11) view, whereas :717 moves CC-CARD-NUM-N, the numeric 9(16) view - and this case drives the card side to zero through that numeric view while the account side carries a non-zero value through its own alphanumeric one, which is the exact converse of case12. The cross-field edit at :637-640 needs FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK AND FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK, so with the account flag ISVALID the NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED condition is never set: 'No input received' must not appear, and neither must 'Account number not provided'. INPUT-ERROR at :360 then sends the map and goes to COMMON-RETURN at :361-363, so 9000-READ-DATA is never reached - and the account named is deliberately one that is PRESENT, zero based row index 2 of the seeded slice carrying account 00000000002, card 0923877193247330, embossed name 'Enrico Rosenbaum', expiry 2024-08-11 and status Y, so an implementation that wrongly fell back to an account-keyed alternate-index lookup would have found a real record and passed silently. Neither repository entry point is invoked - not CardRepository.readByCardNumber for the base key and not readByAccountIdViaAltIndex for the alternate one, since 9150-GETCARD-BYACCT is never performed from anywhere in the program and stays dead code, its only two occurrences being its own label at :779 and its exit label at :810 (gate G45, practice B5) - and the non invocation is asserted where it is observable: CRDNAMEO stays at LOW-VALUES and does NOT carry 'Enrico Rosenbaum', which is precisely the leak this case guards against, while the three seeded rows are asserted byte for byte exactly as seeded with an empty write channel as the other half of that statement. No fixture row carries the typed card 0000000000000000 either, so the base-key read could not have matched even had it been attempted. 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS then paints asymmetrically: EIBCALEN is 172 so the ELSE arm runs; CDEMO-ACCT-ID is 2 and therefore non-zero, so :465 echoes CC-ACCT-ID into ACCTSIDO as '00000000002'; CDEMO-CARD-NUM was zeroed at :700, so :468-469 leaves CARDSIDO at LOW-VALUES and the sixteen zeros the operator typed are NOT echoed back; FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT is false because nothing was read, so CRDNAMEO, CRDSTCDO, EXPMONO and EXPYEARO stay as MOVE LOW-VALUES TO CCRDSLAO left them at :428 - binary zero, not spaces; and WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE at :490 still holds, so WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT puts the thirty-six characters of 'Please enter Account and Card Number' into INFOMSGO PIC X(40). 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS does not arrive from the card list - CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is 'COCRDSL' and LIT-CCLISTMAPSET is 'COCRDLI', so the conjunction at :505-506 is false - which sends both ACCTSIDA and CARDSIDA of the input group to DFHBMFSE at :510-511 and leaves the DFHDFCOL at :529-530 unwritten. The cursor EVALUATE at :515-524 is ordered and arm one is FALSE on both of its conditions, because the account flag is ISVALID rather than NOT-OK or BLANK; arm two therefore wins on the SECOND of its two conditions, FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK, so :521 moves -1 into CARDSIDL and ACCTSIDL is never touched (gate G30). The colour guards then fire exactly once between them: :533 is false because the account flag is ISVALID, :537 is false because the card flag is BLANK and not NOT-OK - the same one byte field carries '0' for NOT-OK, '1' for ISVALID and a space for BLANK at :59-62, and SET FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK at :695 replaced the NOT-OK :688 had set - :541 is false for the account, and only :547-551 runs, moving '*' into CARDSIDO and DFHRED into CARDSIDC. MOVE '*' at :549 space fills its PIC X(16) receiver rather than leaving the LOW-VALUES behind, because a one character literal moved to an alphanumeric item pads on the right - so CARDSIDO is an asterisk followed by fifteen spaces, not an asterisk followed by binary zeros, and not the sixteen zeros that were typed; ACCTSIDC is reported DFHDFCOL because 0x00 is that mnemonic on the colour plane and nothing ever wrote to it, so the valid account carries neither red nor an asterisk. COCRDSLC copies no CSSETATY - only COACTUPC does, and this program's own only include of that kind is CSSTRPFY at :855 - and it re implements the highlight inline with the BLANK path gated on CDEMO-PGM-REENTER and the NOT-OK path ungated, so this case owns a gated blank side of gate G38 on the card field while cases 05, 09 and 10 own the ungated one; flattening the two would silently stop colouring a rejected filter on first entry. INFOMSGC is DFHNEUTR from :556 because 1200 has already filled WS-INFO-MSG. 1400-SEND-SCREEN then moves LIT-THISMAPSET, which is PIC X(8) VALUE 'COCRDSL ' at :167-168, into CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET PIC X(7) - a PIC X receiver truncates on the right, so the surviving mapset is 'COCRDSL' - names CCRDSLA as the map, and sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :567, so the returned context is 1 again; :588 had already named COCRDSLC as CCARD-NEXT-PROG. COMMON-RETURN lays the 160 byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and the twelve byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, which is CA-FROM-PROGRAM PIC X(08) plus CA-FROM-TRANID PIC X(04) at :200-203, into WS-COMMAREA PIC X(2000) and issues EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CCDL') at :402-406, so every byte of conversation state travels in the payload and nothing whatever is retained on the server (gate G37, rule R6). The commarea transition is deliberately observable: the card arrives as 0923877193247330 - the very card the typed account owns, so the context could not have been more helpful - and leaves as sixteen zeros, which is :700 taking effect, while the account arrives as eleven zeros and leaves as 00000000002, which is :676. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:16:00, the instant the source's own version footer carries at app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy:45, so CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are the literals 07/19/22 and 23:16:00 rather than today (practice B7), and the unit is reached as a plain Java object with the fixture backed repository handed to its constructor - no MockMvc and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51). CARDDAT is the only dataset seeded, because CARDAIX is a path over the same base cluster and not a dataset of its own (gate G45), and it is seeded from the derived test copy under src/test/resources/fixtures rather than from app/data/ASCII, which stays read only (practice B3). Two shape notes, both taken from ParityCase rather than from prose: the screen's texts are pinned inside the send rather than in expectedMessages, because that list is reserved for lines a program emits at one of three fixed channel widths and COCRDSL's ERRMSG is PIC X(80) while the screen channel is 78; and the row expectations travel on expectedWrites and expectedFinalState, which are the members the model actually declares. This case also names row index 2 rather than the row its SPACES twin names, because the guard that matters here is that 'Enrico Rosenbaum' must not leak into CRDNAMEO from a read that never happened; the pair discipline is kept on shape, seeded slice, pinned clock and structure. Several gates have no site here: G32, because every GO TO in this program is a forward early exit or the shared COMMON-RETURN and there is no backward loop to restructure; G35, because there is no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere in COCRDSLC, whose abend path is the CICS native HANDLE ABEND at :250-252 into EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE('9999'); G39, because COCRDSL declares no PAGENO and no EXPDAY; G19 and G21, because no record is decoded on a path that never reads; G40 and G47; and rule R4 with gates G22 to G28, because COCRDSLC holds no PIC 9(n)V(n) monetary field at all. The class is named CardSelectController because the migration plan names it so, while the source Function header, README.md:213-231 and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:220 DESCRIPTION(VIEW CARD DETAIL) all describe a card detail view - honoured verbatim per rule R1 and documented rather than corrected per practice B4, register AAP 0.8.4. No user rules govern this repository - review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided' - so the binding constraints on this fixture are the enterprise practices B1, B3, B4, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12 rather than any project rule. Every expected value here was derived by structured reading of app/cbl/COCRDSLC.cbl against the app/cpy-bms/COCRDSL.CPY xxxI and xxxO PICTURE clauses, the app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy 150 byte record layout whose closing FILLER X(59) the seeded images carry, the app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy REDEFINES pairs at CC-ACCT-ID and CC-CARD-NUM, the app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy title literals whose line 21 is commented out and line 22 active, app/bms/COCRDSL.bms and the real US-ASCII fixture whose row at index 2 genuinely carries account 00000000002 and the embossed name Enrico Rosenbaum; none of it was captured from a running COBOL program, because this environment cannot run one - eight blockers are recorded in AAP 0.7.6 and the substitution is escalated as risk R-A (practice B12).
